title: Do natural disasters kill more people than a century ago?
subtitle: Today disasters kill about 45,000 people a year. Guess the 1920s toll, then see why the risk per person fell by about 98 percent.
notes: Now asks for the 1920s bar (2010s shown first) so the starting bar (4 % of the axis) sits far from the truth; axis 0–800, relative tolerance 25 %. EM-DAT decadal averages: 1920s about 524,000 a year (droughts about 472,000, marked by a dashed line), 2010s about 45,400; then the same bars animate to deaths per million people (266 vs 6; population averages 1.97 bn and 7.42 bn) for the −98 %. 2004 (about 246,000) is a label, not a highlight of the 2010s bar. No people/text column any more. The bar chart's y label stays small (engine).
